requiredFindings.title: The shared cfg(test) gates need one predicate that names both features
requiredFindings.failureScenario: Item 4 declares scenario-fixtures and item 4b rewrites existing cfg(test) gates to cfg(any(test, feature = "scenario-fixtures")). The gates scenario calls are the ones accepted X9 r1 item 6 and G1 already assigned to X9-1: Image::Injected (crates/security/src/trust/initial_core.rs, cfg(test) at f1b8321), HomeSource::Fixture and its match arm (crates/security/src/custody/installation_admission.rs), X4T-0 (crates/security/src/trust/accepted_store_fixture.rs), and the fenced state.v1 publisher. X9 pins every such site as cfg(any(test, feature = "crash-matrix")), and a site outside that list is a forbidden substitute. A Rust item has one cfg predicate. Item 4b, implemented as written, drops crash-matrix from the predicate, so X9's synthetic installation, injected image, and signed store do not compile in a crash-matrix build. X9 item 6, implemented as written, leaves scenario::operation unable to name those seams. Required: one site list, X9-1's pin extended by name, each shared site written cfg(any(test, feature = "crash-matrix", feature = "scenario-fixtures")). The list is only the fixture gates both surfaces call. AppendStep, ObjectStep, and the ledger commit hook stay cfg(test), with X9's barrier points beside them. scenario-fixtures stays a separate feature, enabled from storage's and host's [dev-dependencies], so B0–B8 run in cargo test --workspace --all-targets. crash-matrix keeps X9 item 2: no manifest dependency names it, only the matrix targets' required-features enable it, and a release build with the feature fails at compile_error. crash_matrix_support still returns no authority type. scenario::operation still returns the ProjectOperation the production chain returns, and that function is compiled only under scenario-fixtures. X8 records the joint predicate as the wording change to X9 item 6. That record leaves X9's accepted outcome in place. X3d r7's fixture sentence names this same list.

requiredFindings.title: B6 and B7 publish the revocation from the process that holds the lease
requiredFindings.failureScenario: Item 4c's publish_revocation and cases B6 and B7 run on the test thread after the handoff. The handoff has released the fence, and the session still holds the operation lease (X2 r8 item 7a, X4 r7 item 2). X4 item 2 forbids writing trust state under a lease. A publication X4T-b will admit takes the installation fence and is performed by a caller that does not hold that lease; X9 item 6's helper, run as item 11's parent, is that caller. The same-thread call after operation() either takes the fence under the lease or replaces state.v1 with no fence. B6's gate 0 → 2 reading depends on the fenced publication. Required: B6 and B7 publish through that helper, in a process that does not hold the operation lease. The test thread waits for the helper to exit, then calls prepare_commit and publish. There is no sleep. The helper is the shared publisher on the RF-1 site list, so a scenario-fixtures build can run it. B3 and B5 stay on the test thread; they replace project files and do not take the fence.
